title: Three-Dimensional Mapping of Decimation of Breast Cancer Cells by Therapeutic Nanoparticles
content: Drug-resistant cancer cells have been found occurring in significant number in the population the diseased cells that oppose active chemoradiations and surgical resections. The chemotherapy-resistant cancer recurrence and metastasis in many cases can be attributed to autophagy, that indirectly causes tumorigenesis by inducing resistance against chemotherapeutic agents. In this context, inhibiting drug-induced autophagy by multiple-drug infusions are of excellent therapeutic benefits but accompany mephitic side effects and toxicities. To overcome such hurdles, we developed a multi-strategic approach to annihilate breast cancer cells by impairing autophagy and parallel induction of apoptosis. This approach employs the induction of therapeutic gold nanocages (TANs) that encompasses a central gold nanocage (AuNcg) core coated with mauran (MR) polysaccharide, functionalized with 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4OHT) and anti-TROP-2 monoclonal antibodies (MAb) to breast cancer cells (MCF7) resulting in downright decimation of subcellular organelles leading to cell deaths (Fig. 1A) [1]. Its selective nature to destroy only the diseased cells and not impact the healthy ones, moderates side effects to a practical zero along with its excellent carrier capability. Internalized TANs are found to interact primarily with nucleus, mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Herein, we examined the deleterious repercussions of the TANs on these subcellular organelles by employing transmission and volumetric electron microscopes (TEM and VEM) followed by Three-dimensional computational image analysis that revealed previously unknown systemic degradation process leading to complete decimation of the diseased breast cancer cells.
